chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: 'Three things purify a man's love for his Muslim brother: he meets him with cheerfulness when he encounters him, and he makes space for him in the gathering when he comes to sit with him, and he calls him by the name most beloved to him.'

key_terms.الْبُشْر: cheerfulness/brightness of face — implies a radiant, welcoming expression; more than a mere smile, it signifies genuine gladness
key_terms.الْمَجْلِس: the gathering/assembly — a formal or informal seated gathering, a central institution in Arab social life for learning, decision-making, and fellowship
key_terms.وُدّ: affection/love — a deep, warm regard, distinguishable from حب (hub) in that wudd often implies a lasting, demonstrated affection
key_terms.يُصْفِينَ: purify/clarify — from the root ص-ف-و meaning to become pure or clear; the love is 'purified' in the sense of becoming unmixed, wholehearted, and sincere

ai.seo_question: What three things does the Prophet say purify a Muslim's love for his brother?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) identifies three social behaviors that strengthen and purify the bond of fraternal love between Muslims. These practices — greeting with a cheerful face, making physical space in gatherings, and using a person's preferred name — reflect the Prophet's emphasis on cultivating genuine warmth in Islamic community life. The hadith addresses early Muslim communities where social gatherings (majlis) were central to communal life, and the three actions represent active expressions of respect and affection rather than mere passive goodwill.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Three (things) would purify a Muslim’s love for his brother (in Eman) – he meets him with a smile when he does meet him, and makes space for him in the gathering when he comes over to sit, and he calls him with the name most beloved to him’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Three things purify a Muslim’s love for his brother (in belief): meeting him in a cheerful manner, preparing for him a seat if he wants to sit down in a gathering, and calling him by his names that he loves most.’”
